html:
The Second Battle of El Alamein was fought from 23 October to 4 November 1942 in the desert of Egypt, about 100 km west of Alexandria. The British Eighth Army under Bernard Montgomery beat the German and Italian army of Erwin Rommel.

In summer 1942 Rommel drove into Egypt, aiming for the Suez Canal and the oil beyond. He was stopped at El Alamein, a railway halt where the gap between the sea and the soft sands of the Qattara Depression was only about 60 km wide, so no army could go around. Montgomery built up about 195,000 men and 1,000 tanks against 116,000 and about 550. The Axis army was short of fuel, because British ships, aircraft and codebreakers were sinking its supply ships. The attack opened at night with about 900 guns. Infantry cleared paths through deep minefields, and after twelve days of fighting the tanks broke through. Rommel retreated, against Hitler's order.

Days later American and British forces landed in Morocco and Algeria. Caught between two armies, the Axis forces in Africa surrendered in Tunisia in May 1943. It was the first big land victory of the British Empire over Germany in World War II.
sum: The Second Battle of El Alamein was fought from 23 October to 4 November 1942 in the desert of Egypt, about 100 km west of Alexandria. The British Eighth Army under Bernard Montgomery beat the German and Italian army of Erwin Rommel.
